key_insights: US equity leadership remains extremely concentrated in Mag 7. S&P and Nasdaq held up while the Russell struggled, and Asia did not follow the US highs (Korea down 2%, Taiwan flat, HK tech fading). The author reads this as higher oil and higher real rates hurting duration-sensitive parts of the market, not generic risk-off.

European flows were heavily for sale the prior day, with long selling and ETF supply into the rally. Follow-through from oil relief and rates support was limited, which the author links to a widening real rate and equity valuation gap.
Samsung reports preliminary Q3 tomorrow. Results are expected to be very large, and the author argues that if fundamentals keep delivering, the stock earns into its already low multiple.

SpaceX is looking to raise $40bn to buy Nvidia chips. The author sees it as another endorsement of compute demand, but says more leverage in the AI ecosystem is not what the market wants to hear right now.

Marvell's guidance was a strong endorsement of the custom silicon and interconnect chain and supportive for Broadcom. TSMC fundamentals remain very strong. Mistral released a competitive European open-weight model.

Oil: no resolution and the regional conflict is broadening (Houthis attacking Aden, Saudi intercepting a missile near Riyadh), even as physical flows improve. Vitol estimates about 12mbd of crude and 2mbd of products left the Middle East over the last 7-10 days, so the problem is increasingly freight, insurance and logistics rather than barrels.
The author thinks Iran may be drifting toward a frozen conflict. With the midterms approaching, odds of a durable solution before then look slim, though talks appear to continue.

France: Le Pen's fiscal plan (€140bn of net savings by 2032, a constitutional golden rule, deficit under 3% by 2030) cut near-term tail risk in OATs, with yields and spreads falling sharply. Her proposed €5bn cap on France's net EU contribution creates a longer-term institutional risk that matters more for the euro than for OATs.
RBI hiked 25bp to 5.5% and moved to calibrated tightening. The author reads it as the energy shock forcing a global tightening impulse while US front-end expectations calm.

US rates: October Fed hike odds are about 20% versus about 85% for December, yet the 10yr is still near 5.30%. The front end is anchored and the long end is not rallying. The 3yr auction was well absorbed, with the 10yr auction today and the 30yr tomorrow as tests of duration supply. Fed minutes are due later today.
Gold and crypto were softer overnight, which the author takes as confirmation that real rate pressure is still biting.

Positioning: funds have added tech and raised Mag 7 nets, but overall nets remain extremely low and sentiment is pessimistic. The author stays constructive on AI and says the leadership is justified by inference demand and the compute shortage. Bonds, the Russell and Europe need a durable energy solution or rate relief to work, even with positioning as a tailwind.

sector_views.rationale: Author is constructive on AI and says leadership is justified by fundamentals in the inference economy and compute shortage. Marvell guidance and TSMC strength are cited as support.
Positioning is a tailwind, but the author says it is hard for them to work sustainably without a durable energy solution and rate relief.

tension_points.bull_case: SpaceX's $40bn raise to buy Nvidia chips, Marvell's guidance and TSMC strength all endorse compute demand, and the author sees the leadership as justified by the inference economy and compute shortage.
tension_points.bear_case: More leverage in the AI ecosystem is not what the market wants to hear right now, with higher oil and real rates already hitting duration-sensitive assets.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning is a major tailwind and nets are extremely low with pessimistic sentiment.
tension_points.bear_case: It is hard for these to work sustainably without a durable energy solution, and the long end is not rallying despite calmer front-end expectations.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A durable energy solution or rate relief would favor the bull case. The author is watching the Fed minutes, Samsung's results and the 10yr auction.

tension_points.bull_case: Le Pen's savings plan and golden rule took near-term sovereign tail risk out of OATs, with yields and spreads falling sharply.
tension_points.bear_case: Capping the net EU contribution at €5bn points to a government prioritizing national consolidation over EU transfers, a bigger longer-term risk for the euro than for OATs.
